precepts.text: King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel, thirty thousand men, and sent them to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses: a month in Lebanon, two months at home.
precepts.point: The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: “king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.” He levied a tax, and the tax was men.

“And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses: a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.” Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

That is what Samuel told Israel: “He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself.”

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” Nathan was the prophet of David’s day, the one through whom the Lord spoke to David.

Solomon reminds Hiram of what the Lord spoke to David his father: “Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build an house unto my name.” That word came in the time of David, and now Solomon purposes to build the house.

Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.” He slew a giant “when he was yet but young”, and beat down “the boasting of Goliath”, “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.”

David was a man of war from his youth. That is why Solomon tells Hiram that “David my father could not build an house unto the name of the Lord his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet.”

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“So the people honoured him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in that he gave him a crown of glory. For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his adversaries, and brake their horn in sunder unto this day.”

David destroyed the enemies on every side. Those are the wars that were about him on every side, which kept him from building the house, until the Lord put them “under the soles of his feet.” What David fought through, Solomon inherited as rest.

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever.”

That is exactly what Solomon tells Hiram: “But now the Lord my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.” God made all quiet round about him so that he might build the house. So Solomon purposes to build it, and asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, where the best cedar grew, “for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.” The Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation.

precepts.text: Solomon determines to build a house for the name of the Lord and numbers the bearers, hewers, and overseers, sending to Hiram to deal with him as he dealt with David, because the house is for burning incense, showbread, and the offerings on the sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, an ordinance forever for Israel.
precepts.point: This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon was able to say deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built. It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.” He told out “threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

Then he sent to Huram the king of Tyre: “As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.” This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon could say, deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built.

The house was for the name of the Lord, “to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

So Hiram gave cedar and fir, Solomon gave wheat and pure oil year by year, and “there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.” It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

precepts.text: Hiram answers in writing, blessing the Lord God of Israel, and sends a cunning man named Huram whose father was a man of Tyre and whose mother was of the daughters of Dan, skillful to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, and fine linen, showing that Hiram and his craftsman were joined to Israel by lineage.
precepts.point: This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon was able to say deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built. It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the Lord hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them.” He said, “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.”

Hiram sent “a cunning man, endued with understanding”, “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson”.

Hiram and his craftsman were joined to Israel by lineage: the craftsman’s mother was of the daughters of Dan. That is part of why there was peace between Hiram and Solomon and they two made a league together, and why “the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him” is seen in how he dealt with Hiram.

precepts.text: Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, with three thousand six hundred to oversee them, the same ordered labor described here.
precepts.point: Solomon had order in the work, with bearers of burdens, hewers in the mountains, and above them the chief of his officers, thirty-three hundred who ruled over the people that wrought. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure without murmuring over who did which task.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom. And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

That is the same ordered labor described here: “threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains”, and over them the chief of Solomon’s officers, “which ruled over the people that wrought in the work.” Solomon had order in the work, bearers, hewers and overseers.

The levy was an enlistment for service, thirty thousand men sent to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses, “a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home”, gathered to bring the wood back to Jerusalem, with Adoniram over the levy. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure, without murmuring over who did which task.

precepts.text: Hiram king of Tyre was ever a lover of David, and he sent his servants unto Solomon, helping to supply the timber for the building of the temple.
precepts.point: David prepared iron in abundance for the nails and for the joinings, brass in abundance without weight, and cedar trees in abundance. The Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 22: David Prepares to Build the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.” Hiram helped supply the timber for the building of the temple.

That help was already coming in David's day. David gathered the strangers in the land of Israel and set masons to hew stones for the house of God, and prepared iron, brass and “cedar trees in abundance: for the Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.” The strangers were brought in to help build the temple, and Tyre, whose king loved David, kept on helping his son.

points: Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants to Solomon because he had heard that Solomon was anointed king in the room of his father. Hiram was ever a lover of David, so the friendship carries over to the son.
Hiram was king of Tyre, a Zidonian by his father and connected by lineage to the tribe of Naphtali on his mother's side, which is drawn out later in the reading.
